akhfash:4-4.t: He said ﴿مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾: it is really "Allah has not made for a man two hearts in his chest"; ﴿مِنْ﴾ came for tawkīd (emphasis), just as you say "رأيتُ زَيْداً نَفْسَهُ" (I saw Zayd himself); so he brought in "مِنْ" for emphasis.

akhfash:5-5.t: And He said ﴿ٱدْعُوهُمْ لآبَآئِهِمْ﴾ because you say "هو يُدْعَى لفلان" (he is called after so-and-so).

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَفْعَلُوۤاْ﴾: in the position of the accusative, an exception falling outside (the first part).

akhfash:10-10.t: And He said ﴿ٱلظُّنُونَاْ﴾: the Arabs append wāw, yāʾ and alif at the end of rhymes, and they likened the verse-endings to that.

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿وَإِذاً لاَّ تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: you put what follows "إِذَاً" in the indicative because of the wāw, and likewise the fāʾ. He said ﴿فإِذاً لا يُؤْتُونَ النَّاسَ تَفسِيرا﴾; in some readings it is subjunctive: they made it operate as they make it operate without fāʾ or wāw. «[Translator's note: so in the text; the verse is Q 4:53 «فإذاً لا يؤتون الناس نقيرا».]»

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿وَلَـٰكِن رَّسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ﴾, i.e. but he was the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.

akhfash:52-52.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ أَن تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is "that you exchange them for (other) wives"; ﴿مِنْ﴾ was brought in for emphasis.

akhfash:53-53.t:
And He said ﴿وَلاَ مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ﴾: he conjoined it to ﴿غَيْر﴾ and so made it accusative, or to what follows ﴿غَيْر﴾ and so made it genitive.
And He said ﴿لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "unless you are given permission, not waiting". It cannot be genitive (as an attribute) of "the food" unless you say "أَنْتُمْ" (you). Do you not see that if you said: "ائذَن لعبد الله على امرأة مبغضا لها" (give ʿAbd Allāh permission to enter on a woman, hating her), only the accusative would be possible in it, unless you said "مبغض لها هو" (hating her, he)? Because if you make his attribute run on her (as an attribute of her) and do not make overt the pronoun that shows the attribute belongs to him, it is not (correct) speech. If you said: "هذا رَجُلٌ مَعَ امْرَأةٍ ملازِمها" (this is a man with a woman, keeping close to her), it would be a solecism until you say "مُلازِمُها" in the nominative, or say "ملازِمِها هُوَ" in the genitive.

akhfash:56-56.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلاَئِكَـتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ صَلُّواْ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسْلِيماً﴾: people's ṣalāt upon him is their supplication for him, and the ṣalāt of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the spreading of good about him.

akhfash:60-60.t: [And He said] ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾, i.e. "they will not be your neighbours in it except a little", as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
